summary: The change fixes cipherstash/stack#1045: OidcFederationStrategy used to hand one cached CTS token to every caller, so on a shared server a user's lock-context encryptions could be bound to another user's identity. It now asks the provider on every get_token, keys a bounded LRU of refresh engines on the SHA-256 of the whole JWT, stamps persisted tokens with that digest and serves stored tokens only to the matching JWT, adds getTokenForJwt and a cacheCapacity option to the napi, wasm and Go bindings, and moves the JS getJwt call into the caller's async context. The Rust core is closely and adversarially tested (forged-signature, concurrency, cancellation, refusal tests), though no test was run here. The main residual risk is guidance: docs and shipped agent skills now say one module-level strategy serves every user, but on the @cipherstash/stack native path protect-ffi calls getToken through a Neon Channel bound to the context that built the client, so an AsyncLocalStorage-based getJwt can silently read the wrong request (the same identity-binding failure the PR fixes); the caveat describes this only as the request being 'not visible' and no test covers that path. Secondary risks are CTS exchange volume and strategy-wide usage-limit lockouts when IdPs rotate JWTs often, and one-time cookie/store misses on upgrade.

behaviour_changes.description: OidcProvider::fetch / getJwt is now called on every get_token (every ZeroKMS operation), not only when the cached CTS token needs renewal, and must return the current caller's JWT. Breaking for providers that are expensive or return a fixed JWT.

Tokens are cached per distinct provider JWT (SHA-256 of the whole JWT) in a bounded LRU (default 1024) plus a pending tier; a refused exchange takes no slot; account-level refusals (usage limit, unprovisioned org) are remembered strategy-wide for 60 s and answer every new JWT without an exchange.

Federated tokens carry a new optional federated_from field (hex SHA-256 of the JWT) in their persisted JSON; a TokenStore-loaded token is served only to the JWT whose digest it carries; unstamped tokens stored by earlier releases are cache misses.

@cipherstash/auth Node and wasm-inline OidcFederationStrategy instances get a getToken() that awaits getJwt in the JS caller's async context and calls a new public getTokenForJwt(jwt); create/createWithStore take an optional trailing cacheCapacity. Go gains stackauth.WithCacheCapacity.

Shipped agent skills (stash-auth, stash-edge, stash-encryption, stash-supabase), READMEs and typings change guidance from 'one Encryption() client per request/user' to 'one long-lived/module-level strategy serves every user', with a caveat for the @cipherstash/stack native client path.
stack-auth adds sha2 0.10; root and detached workspace lockfiles (eql, fuzz, Go guests) updated.

failure_scenarios.title: Stack native client with a shared strategy runs getJwt in the client-creation request's context and binds users to the wrong identity
failure_scenarios.trigger: An app follows the new guidance ('a module-level strategy is fine', 'one strategy serves every user') with an AsyncLocalStorage-based getJwt (Clerk auth(), Next.js headers()) and lazily builds a shared @cipherstash/stack Encryption() client inside its first request.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: protect-ffi stores the strategy's getToken (now the index.js own-property wrapper that awaits getJwt) and invokes it through a Neon Channel obtained from the JS context that called newClient (protect-ffi lib.rs 508-575). The PR's own reasoning for the napi ThreadsafeFunction is that such callbacks run in the async context where they were created; if the Channel behaves the same, getJwt reads the ALS store of the request that built the client on every later call. The per-JWT cache then faithfully returns the first user's token for every user. The docs/skills caveat describes this path only as the request being 'not visible', which suggests a loud failure, whereas this variant is silent. The added Node test covers only a strategy created outside any scope via the raw native getToken, not the stack/protect-ffi path or a client created inside a scope.
failure_scenarios.consequence: User B's ZeroKMS operations are authorised as user A; values encrypted under a lock context are bound to A's identity, so B cannot decrypt them and A can, with no error. This is the #1045 failure, reached through guidance this change introduced.

existing_verification.description: oidc-federation-strategy.test.ts: getToken() from two ALS scopes on a module-level strategy gets each caller's subject; raw native getToken from a third scope fails 'no request in scope'.

missing_verification: An end-to-end test of @cipherstash/stack Encryption() with a shared OidcFederationStrategy and an ALS-based getJwt, with the client created both outside and inside a request scope, asserting each operation's token subject.

failure_scenarios.mitigation: Until cipherstash/stack#1065 lands, keep the stack-facing guidance at 'build the client per request / capture req in the closure' without the 'module-level strategy is fine' framing nearby, and state that on this path getJwt may see the wrong request rather than none; or have the stack client snapshot the JWT in the caller's context per operation before crossing into protect-ffi.

failure_scenarios.title: Frequent JWT rotation multiplies CTS exchanges and a usage-limit refusal locks out every rotating user for 60 s
failure_scenarios.trigger: An identity provider whose session JWTs are short-lived and re-minted often (or a getJwt/OAuth2 token source that mints per call) on a server with many active users.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The cache key is the whole JWT, so every rotation is a new engine and a POST /api/authorise; previously one strategy made one exchange per CTS token lifetime. When CTS answers an exchange with UsageLimitExceeded or OrgNotProvisioned, settle() records a strategy-wide StickyDenial and engine_for() returns it for every new JWT for the window, while only users whose exact JWT is cached keep working.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Higher auth latency and CTS load proportional to users x rotations; if that load trips a usage limit, all users whose JWT rotated in the next minute fail encryption/decryption operations. Availability degradation, not data corruption.

failure_scenarios.title: Stored tokens from earlier releases, mixed-version deploys and shared stores miss the cache
failure_scenarios.trigger: Upgrade of @cipherstash/auth with existing cookies/TokenStores, a rolling deploy with old and new instances sharing a store, or a store shared by several users (e.g. Redis).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: BoundStore::load returns None unless the stored token's federated_from matches the caller's digest; old releases write unstamped tokens and (Token has no deny_unknown_fields) ignore the stamp on read, so during a mixed deploy new instances keep missing tokens written by old ones, and old ones still serve any stored token to any caller as before.
failure_scenarios.consequence: One extra exchange per user after upgrade, repeated re-exchange while versions are mixed, and effectively no store caching for a store shared across users. Old instances retain the pre-fix cross-user behaviour until fully replaced.

missing_verification: No test of a token stamped by the new release being read by the previous release.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Complete rollouts promptly (old instances keep #1045); document that a shared store caches only the most recent user (already in the changeset).

Reword the stack-path caveat in stash-auth, stash-encryption, READMEs and the stack docstring to say getJwt may observe the request that created the client (silent wrong user), and keep 'build the client per request' as the rule for the stack native entry until #1065.
Reviewer to confirm Neon Channel async-context semantics in protect-ffi on supported Node versions and whether getToken lookup binds to the wrapper's own property.
Watch /api/authorise rate and UsageLimitExceeded responses per workspace after release; consider info-level or metric counters for exchanges and evictions.
Run the stack-auth (--features http), @cipherstash/auth (Node and wasm) and Go stackauth suites in CI and attach results before release.
Roll out services fully rather than leaving mixed versions sharing a store, since old instances keep the cross-user behaviour and new ones re-exchange their unstamped tokens.

evidence.claim: get_token calls provider.fetch() on every call and then get_token_for_jwt, which looks up/creates an engine per JWT and settles the outcome.
engine_for keys on JwtDigest, uses cache then pending, returns a fresh strategy-wide denial before creating an engine; settle records account refusals for all JWTs.
Bounded LRU; at capacity evicts least recently used with a debug log; capacity 0 retains nothing.
BoundStore::load serves a stored token only when federated_from matches the caller's digest; otherwise None.
Token gains serde-default, skip-if-none federated_from; no deny_unknown_fields on Token.
OidcProvider doc: called on every get_token; a provider that mints a new JWT per call exchanges per call and takes a cache slot each time.
JwtDigest is SHA-256 of the whole JWT; matches_hex compares lowercase hex.
ownGetJwt defines an own-property getToken on the instance that awaits getJwt and calls getTokenForJwt.

Test covers a strategy created outside any ALS scope: wrapper getToken sees each scope; raw native getToken fails 'no request in scope'. No case where the creating call is inside a scope, and no stack/protect-ffi path.
Shipped skill says one long-lived strategy serves many users and a module-level strategy is fine; caveat says on the stack native path the request's ALS is 'not visible' inside getJwt.
Root README example says one strategy serves every user, with the 'not visible' caveat for the native entry.
Stack docstring: client calls the strategy from a background task (Neon channel); capture req or build the client per request until #1065.
NeonJsAuthStrategy looks up the strategy object's getToken property and keeps a Channel from the calling JS context, invoking getToken from tokio tasks on every ZeroKMS request.
wasm-inline getToken awaits #getJwt in the caller's context and calls the binding's getTokenForJwt.
sha2 0.10 added to stack-auth dependencies; lockfiles updated in detached workspaces.
WithCacheCapacity option added and passed as cache_capacity in the OIDC guest config; provider documented as called on every Token call.
Rust tests cover cross-user isolation, forged-signature JWT, per-call provider, LRU eviction, zero capacity, store stamping/misses, concurrency, cancellation and account-refusal memory.
